source_caption:
📺 That ’70s Show (1998–2006)

That ‘70s Show follows Eric Forman, a sarcastic and awkward teenager growing up in the fictional town of Point Place, Wisconsin, during the 1970s. Alongside his closest friends Donna Pinciotti, Michael Kelso, Jackie Burkhart, Steven Hyde, and Fez, Eric navigates the hilarious challenges of adolescence, first love, friendships, family expectations, and growing up. Much of the group’s adventures take place in Eric’s basement, where they spend their time hanging out, making questionable decisions, and getting into unforgettable situations. Meanwhile, Eric’s strict father Red and loving mother Kitty bring their own hilarious personalities to the household, creating endless family conflicts and memorable moments. Starring Topher Grace, Mila Kunis, Ashton Kutcher, Laura Prepon, Danny Masterson, Wilmer Valderrama, Kurtwood Smith, and Debra Jo Rupp, the series became one of television’s most beloved sitcoms, combining nostalgic 1970s culture, hilarious comedy, complicated romances, and heartwarming stories about friendship, family, and growing up.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Romance • Teen Sitcom • Coming-of-Age

⭐ IMDb: 8.1/10

⏱️ Runtime: Approximately 22 minutes per episode • TV-14

🎥 Creators: Bonnie Turner, Terry Turner & Mark Brazill

📺 Seasons: 8 • 200 Episodes

📚 Spin-Off: That ’90s Show (2023–2024)

🏆 Awards: Winner of a Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Costume Design for a Series.

📺 Where to Watch: Peacock (United States)

source_details.title: That '70s Show
source_details.synopsis: That '70s Show is an American television teen sitcom that aired on Fox from August 23, 1998, to May 18, 2006. The series focuses on the lives of a group of six teenage friends living in the fictional town of Point Place, Wisconsin, from 1976 to 1979. The ensemble cast features Topher Grace, Mila Kunis, Ashton Kutcher, Danny Masterson, Laura Prepon, Wilmer Valderrama, Lisa Robin Kelly, Debra Jo Rupp, Kurtwood Smith, Don Stark, Tommy Chong, and Tanya Roberts. In 1999, the show was remade for the ITV network in the United Kingdom as Days Like These using almost verbatim scripts with minor changes to cultural references.
